validity.recommendation: split ownership by section; Gazprom PJSC at 100 percent fits only the Russian stretch; find the Ukrainian section owner and operator
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. A Kursk encyclopedia entry, Ukrainian Wikipedia and a 2022 Interfax report on Gazprom's rebuild of a 40 km stretch all name it. It is a transmission trunk, so classification is fine. The row crosses from Ukraine to Russia, but Gazprom owns only the Russian side. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the two sections now work separately. No source was found that names the Ukrainian owner or operator.

validity.recommendation: change StartYear1 from 1960 to 1959; record diameters as 700, 800, 1020 mm or add a note; capacity of 13 is unsupported
validity.researcher_notes: Start year: a Kursk encyclopedia entry and a second Russian source put the end of construction and start of operation in 1959. Gas reached Belgorod in 1958 per Ukrainian Wikipedia. The 1960 in Wikipedia is about gas reaching Kyiv over another line. Diameter: Ukrainian Wikipedia gives a 700 mm first line, an 800 mm second line and 1020 mm looping, so the sheet's single 1020 mm is only one of them. Capacity of 13 million cubic meters per day is not backed by any source found.

validity.recommendation: no duplicate; it shares the Shebelinka start only with P3381 and P3382, which end at Slovyansk
validity.researcher_notes: Checked against the roster. P3381 and P3382 (Shebelinka to Slovyansk, 70 and 54 km) are different corridors. No other row shares both endpoints. Ukrainian Wikipedia says its Ukrainian part together with the Shebelinka to Kharkiv line supplies Kharkiv, so any overlap with a Shebelinka to Kharkiv spur is a spur, not this row.

fills.researcher_notes: The sheet says 1960. A Kursk encyclopedia entry says pipe laying ended in July 1959 and operation began in November or December 1959. A second source says construction ended and industrial use began in 1959. Ukrainian Wikipedia says gas reached Belgorod in 1958. The only 1960 in the Wikipedia text is about gas reaching Kyiv over a different line. Proposed change from 1960 to 1959.

Searched Russian and Ukrainian terms for the line with capacity, plus the Wikipedia, Kursk encyclopedia, Interfax and reconstruction pages. None states a capacity for this line. The Wikipedia page gives only a working pressure of 5.5 MPa. The 13 million cubic meters per day on the sheet is not confirmed.

Ukrainian Wikipedia states the route length is 507 km, which matches the sheet exactly. It is the only source found, so medium tier. A Russian student page gives a very different figure of about 540 000 km, which is plainly a typo and was not used.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources say the line runs from the Shebelinka field in Kharkiv Oblast through Belgorod and Kursk to Bryansk. The sheet's end location cell is blank and is filled with Bryansk. Occupied or not, the start is in Ukraine.

Interfax (October 2022) says the Russian stretch is served by Gazprom Transgaz Moscow. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the Ukrainian and Russian sections run separately. No source was found that names the operator of the Ukrainian section. The operator site tsoua.com blocks automated access and no archived page listing this line was found. One operator for the whole line would be wrong, so none is staged.

The sheet says Gazprom PJSC owns 100 percent. Gazprom does not own the Ukrainian section. Sources show the Ukrainian and Russian sections run separately, with Gazprom Transgaz Moscow serving the Russian stretch. No document was found that states ownership of either section. See the validity note.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest evidence is Ukrainian Wikipedia, last edited January 2025, which describes the Ukrainian section as working and supplying Kharkiv, and a 2022 Interfax report on the Russian section. No source dated 2024 or later states flow on the Ukrainian section after Russian transit ended on 1 January 2025. Searched in Ukrainian and Russian. Kept as operating with no change proposed.

summary: "Real Shebelinka to Bryansk trunk; concerns: start year 1959 not 1960, diameters 700/800/1020, Gazprom 100% owner only fits Russian side; capacity, operator, owner unresolved"
